meta.titre: The 1959 Southern Cameroons Elections: why the KNDP defeated the KNC/KPP alliance
meta.sous_theme: Parties, issues and results of the 1959 elections in the British Southern Cameroons

sections.contenu_markdown: In January 1959 voters in the British Southern Cameroons went to the polls and removed the government that had led the territory since the 1950s. The result put John Ngu Foncha in office and opened the road to the plebiscite of 1961. Examiners like this topic because it joins the history of parties, leaders and ordinary voters to the question of how the territory chose its future. You must be able to explain the positions of the parties, the reasons for the result and the part played by Dr Endeley.

items: Southern Cameroons was administered by Britain under United Nations trusteeship and was governed as part of Nigeria until it received its own regional government in 1954.
A plebiscite is a vote by all qualified citizens on a single question.
Political parties offer different policies on the future of a territory and compete for votes.
The Republic of Cameroon, the former French Cameroons, became independent in 1960.

sections.titre: The 1959 elections in the Southern Cameroons
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The parties and their positions
| Party | Leader | Position on the future |
|---|---|---|
| Kamerun National Congress (KNC) | Dr E. M. L. Endeley | Governed the territory; favoured a close future with Nigeria |
| Kamerun People's Party (KPP) | A party that split from the KNC earlier | Allied with the KNC in the 1959 elections |
| Kamerun National Democratic Party (KNDP) | John Ngu Foncha | Founded in 1955 after Foncha left the KNC; opposed to continued ties with Nigeria and favoured secession, with the final future to be decided later |

A smaller party, One Kamerun, also demanded reunification with the French Cameroons.

### The result
The KNDP won a narrow majority in the House of Assembly. Foncha replaced Endeley as head of government in 1959. The United Nations then arranged plebiscites, and in February 1961 the Southern Cameroons voted to join the Republic of Cameroon.

### Why the KNDP won
| Factor | Explanation |
|---|---|
| The question of Nigeria | Many voters feared domination by Nigerians, especially Igbo, in trade, jobs and politics, and distrusted the KNC's friendly attitude |
| Weaknesses of the government | The KNC/KPP was seen as arrogant and out of touch after years in office, and the alliance looked like a marriage of convenience |
| Regional support | The KNDP was strong in the Grassfields of Bamenda, a densely populated area, while the KNC's strength lay mainly in the coastal and forest areas |
| Leadership and campaign | Foncha ran an energetic campaign with a clear message and presented himself as a protector of Southern Cameroons identity |

### Endeley's part in his defeat
Several causes lay in Endeley's own choices: his friendly attitude to Nigeria, the alliance with the KPP, his government's remoteness from many voters, and failure to read the mood in the Grassfields. Other causes were beyond his control: the strength of Foncha's campaign and regional loyalties. A good answer weighs both groups before judging 'to what extent'.

variantes.nom: Question on the reasons for the KNDP victory
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for causes or factors of the KNDP win.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Group the reasons (the Nigerian question, weaknesses of the KNC/KPP, regional support, Foncha's campaign), explain each with evidence, and rank them.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how far a leader caused a result.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Divide the causes into those controlled by the leader and those outside his control, weigh them, and give a verdict. In a question that asks which factor was NOT a cause, test each factor against the evidence before choosing.

sections.enonce_markdown: How far was the leadership of John Ngu Foncha responsible for the success of the KNDP at the polls in 1959?

etapes.justification: 'How far' needs a judgement about degree.
etapes.resultat_markdown: I must weigh Foncha's leadership against other causes.
Foncha founded the KNDP in 1955, gave it a clear programme of ending ties with Nigeria and ran an active campaign, especially in the Grassfields.

etapes.justification: A balanced answer needs the rest of the evidence.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Many voters feared Nigerian, especially Igbo, domination; the KNC/KPP alliance was seen as arrogant and as an opportunist alliance; regional support in the populous Grassfields favoured the KNDP.

etapes.justification: Weighing means saying which cause depended on which.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Foncha's skill was important because he turned the fear of Nigeria and discontent with the government into votes. Without those feelings his leadership would have had less effect.
Foncha's leadership was a major but not the only cause.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer (key points)**: Foncha's leadership was largely responsible for the KNDP victory because he founded the party, gave it a clear programme and campaigned effectively, especially in the Grassfields. But the result also depended on the fear of Nigerian domination, the unpopularity of the KNC/KPP alliance and regional loyalties. Foncha's skill lay in turning these feelings into votes, so his leadership was an important cause working together with others.

items.erreur_markdown: "The 1959 elections decided that Southern Cameroons would join the Republic of Cameroon."
items.pourquoi_faux: The elections decided who would govern. The future of the territory was decided in the plebiscite of 1961.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the 1959 result brought Foncha to power and that the plebiscite of 1961 decided the future.

items.erreur_markdown: "Endeley and Foncha belonged to the same party in 1959."
items.pourquoi_faux: Foncha left the KNC and founded the KNDP in 1955.
items.correction_markdown: Write that Endeley led the KNC (allied with the KPP) and Foncha led the KNDP.

items.erreur_markdown: Explaining the result with only one cause.
items.pourquoi_faux: Examiners expect several linked causes and a comparison.
items.correction_markdown: Give at least three causes, explain each and say which was the most important.

items.erreur_markdown: Telling the story of the campaign without weighing the causes.
items.pourquoi_faux: A 'how far' or 'account for' question asks for a judgement, and a narrative earns few marks.
items.correction_markdown: Turn each event into a cause, explain its effect on voters, and finish by ranking the causes.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the leader of the KNDP and the leader of the KNC in 1959.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each: **John Ngu Foncha (KNDP)**; **Dr E. M. L. Endeley (KNC)**.

items.enonce_markdown: Account for the success of the KNDP at the polls in the Southern Cameroons in 1959.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for developed points: (1) opposition to continued ties with Nigeria and fear of Nigerian domination; (2) the KNC/KPP was seen as arrogant and as an opportunist alliance; (3) the KNDP had strong support in the populous Grassfields; (4) Foncha's campaign. **The answer should group the causes and say which was most important.**

items.enonce_markdown: To what extent was the 1959 result a vote against Nigeria rather than a vote for the KNDP?
items.solution_markdown: Plan: For the view: fear of Nigerian domination and distrust of the KNC's friendly attitude to Nigeria. Against: the KNDP had a clear programme, an effective leader and organisation, and regional support; the government's own weaknesses also counted. Judgement: **the result was both, and feeling against Nigeria was important but needed the KNDP and Foncha to become votes.**

items_markdown: The KNC under Dr Endeley (allied with the KPP) governed the territory; the KNDP under Foncha was founded in 1955.
The KNDP opposed continued ties with Nigeria; the KNC favoured a close future with Nigeria.
The KNDP won a narrow majority in January 1959 and Foncha replaced Endeley.
Reasons: the Nigerian question, the unpopularity of the KNC/KPP, regional support in the Grassfields and Foncha's campaign.
The election chose a government; the plebiscite of February 1961 decided the future of the territory.
For 'to what extent' questions, weigh the leader's own mistakes against causes outside his control.
